CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
  Tuesday, January 16, 2024 - 6:30 P.M.

How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, January 16, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Chan
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF NEW COMMUNITY EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAM
  (CERT) MEMBERS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of December 19, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – DECEMBER 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-2024 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for December 2023.

  D. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH CALIFORNIA CONSULTING
  FOR GRANT WRITING SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $55,200 ANNUALLY

  On June 6, 2023, the City Council adopted the 2023-24 Fiscal Year budget that
  included $50,000 earmarked for grant writing services. In September 2023, staff
  provided a Request for Proposal to six qualified grant writing consultants. Based
  on proposals received, staff is recommending California Consulting for a one-
  year term at a monthly retainer cost of $4,600. The Fiscal Year 2023-24 general
  fund non-departmental budget includes $50,000 for grant writing services. For
  Fiscal Year 2024-25, the agreement will be budgeted at the full contract
  agreement rate of $4,600 per month or $55,200 annually.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with California Consulting for Grant Writing Services and authorize
  the City Manager to execute the agreement and issue a purchase order in the
  amount of $50,000.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  3
   E. ORDINANCE NO. 699 APPROVING AN ANNEXATION AND PRE-ZONING
  AT 5623 NORTH GLADYS AVENUE (ANX23-001/ZC23-001/GPA23-001) –
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 699 would approve an annexation and pre-zoning
  at 5623 North Gladys Avenue. The Fiscal Year 2023-24 Adopted Budget
  includes the cost for required legal publication and codification of the
  ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments would be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) under Section 15319 (Annexations of Existing Facilities and Lots for
  Exempt Facilities) of the CEQA guidelines. Annexations to a city or special district
  of areas containing existing facilities public or private structures developed to the
  density allowed by the current zoning or pre-zoning of either the gaining or losing
  governmental agency, whichever is more restrictive, provided, however, that the
  extension of utility services to the existing facilities would a capacity to serve only
  the existing facilities.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  699 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case Nos. ANX23-001, GPA23-001, and ZC23-
  001, Approving an annexation and pre-zoning at 5623 North Gladys Avenue.

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 700: AMENDING AN EXISTING PLANNED
  DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY ZONE AND APPROVING A DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENT FOR A MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT AT 201-217 SOUTH SAN
  GABRIEL BOULEVARD (ZC22-001 AND DA22-001) – SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 700 would amend an existing Planned
  Development Overlay Zone and approve a Development Agreement for a
  mixed-use development (Rubio Village). The Fiscal Year 2023-24 Adopted
  Budget includes the cost for required legal publication and codification of the
  ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  project was reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA). The City prepared an Initial Study (IS) to determine the proposed
  project's potential impact on the environment. The City has determined that the
  project may have a significant effect on the environment, but by implementing

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  4
   the identified mitigation measures, the project's impacts could be reduced to less
  than significant levels. Ten mitigation measures have been identified to reduce
  these potential impacts to a less than significant level. The Mitigation Monitoring
  and Reporting Program (MMRP) contains the full text of the mitigation measures,
  as well as identifies the responsible party for implementation and timing.

  The 30-day public review period of the Initial Study/Mitigated Negative
  Declaration was initiated on August 24, 2023, and ended on September 22, 2023.
  A notice regarding the CEQA comment period was posted with the Los Angeles
  County Recorder, published in the San Gabriel Sun newspaper, and distributed to
  relevant regulatory agencies. Additionally, a notice was mailed to owners and
  occupants within 500-feet of the project site. A total of three comment letters
  were submitted to the City during the public comment period. The comment
  letters and the Lead Agency response to comments received are included in the
  Final Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  700 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case Nos. ZC22-001 and DA22-001, Amending
  an Existing Planned Development Overlay Zone and Approving a Development
  Agreement for a Mixed-Use Development at 201-217 South San Gabreil
  Boulevard.”

  G. HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION
  PROPOSED 2024 ANNUAL WORK PLAN

  This is the 2024 Annual Workplan developed by the Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR) Commission for the 2024 calendar year. The Commissioners
  have had open and constructive dialogue to develop a plan that best fits in
  alignment with the goals and scope of the HEAR Commission as well as the City
  of San Gabriel’s Mission. The Commission estimates needing $6,000 from the
  general fund in order to offer the proposed programs/events. Staff will bring
  the budget request at the mid-year budget with the exception of the All Are
  Welcome Program which will be presented to Council separately and the
  corresponding budget request will be made at that time.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  5
   Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the HEAR Commission’s
  Annual Workplan, as presented above, for 2024. If Council would like to make
  any changes to the workplan, they can pull the item from consent and then
  discuss and adopt any changes.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION AND DIRECTION ON A NEW SISTER CITY
  AND FRIENDSHIP CITY POLICY FOR THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL

  This past July, the City Council discussed the possibility of forming new Sister
  City or Friendship City relationships and directed staff to return with a draft
  policy to govern how future requests are handled. Staff has drafted a proposed
  policy based upon examples from other cities and recommends that the City
  Council discuss the proposed policy and provide input and direction on how to
  proceed. There is no fiscal impact associated with a discussion and adoption of
  a policy to guide future Sister and Friendship City relationships. Should the City
  Council decide to consider additional partnerships or to rekindle the ones with
  the current cities, the fiscal impact would be minimal and included in annual
  City budgets. Any larger expenditures would need to be considered and
  approved on a case-to-case basis by the City Council in the future.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the Sister and Friendship City
  policy and after providing any input and changes, adopt the policy.

  Alternatives Recommendations

  In addition to the recommended action, the City Council has the following
  options:

  1. Discuss the proposed policy and provide direction on changes to be
  brought back for future consideration.
  2. Decide not to adopt a policy at this time and direct staff to bring back any
  future Sister City or Friendship City requests for consideration on a case-by-
  case basis.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  6
   3. Decide not to adopt a policy at this time and direct staff to not pursue any
  future Sister City or Friendship City relationships.
  4. Some other action that the City Council decides based upon discussion at
  the meeting.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AUTHORIZATION OF AN ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE AND PROPERTY
  TECHNICIAN (EPT)

  Staff researched the feasibility of the addition of a second Evidence and
  Property Technician. For San Gabriel’s Police Department, as of 2023,
  processing and handling of evidence has expanded to include body worn
  camera footage that is frequently requested by the Los Angeles County District
  Attorney’s Office, attorneys, public, and the media. Producing this discoverable
  footage is a tedious and labor-intensive process that must be completed within
  a small window of time. Approval of this proposal by the City Council would
  result in greater operational efficiency with daily tasks and would help to meet
  the growing demand of public discovery. There is no fiscal impact to the fiscal
  2023-24 budget, but will be included in the fiscal year 2024-25 budget. The
  fiscal impact for the additional Evidence and Property Technician would be
  approximately $101,368.00 per year at fiscal 2023-24 rates.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-01 and
  authorize the City Manager to approve the addition of a second Evidence and
  Property Technician for the San Gabriel Police Department.

  B. PRESENTATION AND ACCEPTANCE OF THE ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE
  FINANCIAL REPORT AND OTHER AUDIT REPORTS FOR THE FISCAL YEAR
  ENDED JUNE 30, 2023

  The certified public accounting firm of Moss, Levy, Hartzheim, LLP (MLH) was
  engaged by the City Council to perform an audit of the financial statements
  and conduct compliance testing of the City of San Gabriel for the fiscal year
  ended June 30, 2023. MLH conducted the audit in accordance with generally
  accepted auditing standards and issued an unqualified (clean) audit opinion on
  the financial statements. This report provides a summary of the audit report to

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  7
   be used as a companion to the published Annual Comprehensive Financial
  Report.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the annual audit reports
  for fiscal year ended June 30, 2023.

  C. ADOPTION OF URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 701 PURSUANT TO
  CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65858 PROHIBITING THE
  ESTABLISHMENT OF MEDICINAL CANNABIS DELIVERY BUSINESSES FOR
  45 DAYS AND AN EXEMPTION FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT

  The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 1186 (SB 1186) in 2022, entitled
  the Medicinal Cannabis Patient’s Right of Access Act, which precluded cities and
  counties from adopting or enforcing regulations that prohibit or have the effect
  of prohibiting the retail sale of medicinal cannabis by delivery. SB 1186 took
  effect on January 1, 2024. In order to provide the City time to adopt reasonable
  regulations for such uses, a 45-day moratorium is necessary. There is no fiscal
  impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Environmental
  review is not required under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to the California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Chapter 3, Sections
  15060(c)(2) (the activity will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable
  indirect physical change in the environment) and 15060(c)(3) (the activity is not
  a project as defined in Section 15378) of the CEQA Guidelines, Cal. Code of Regs,
  Title 14, Chapter 3, because it has no potential to result in a physical change to
  the environment, directly or indirectly. This is because the moratorium adopted
  by the proposed interim ordinance merely prohibits uses that have significant
  impacts on public health, safety, and welfare and does not permit any
  development that could result in a significant change to the environment.
  Furthermore, the moratorium established by the proposed ordinance is
  temporary pending further study and investigation. In addition, the proposed
  ordinance is categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15308 of the
  CEQA Guidelines because this ordinance is a regulatory action taken by the City
  in accordance with Government Code Section 65858 to assure maintenance and
  protection of the environment pending further review of the potential impacts of

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 16, 2024  8
   medical marijuana facilities and mobile medical marijuana dispensaries in the
  City and potential modifications to the San Gabriel Municipal Code.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the proposed Ordinance by at
  least a four-fifths vote.

  Alternative Option:

  Do not adopt the Urgency Ordinance. This will leave the City vulnerable to
  dispensary operators entering the City without any established regulations or
  restrictions on location.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, February 6, 2023 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

Materials Available for Inspection. You may view agenda items online at

Council after distribution of the Agenda packet, will be posted on the City website.

MINUTES OF JANUARY 16, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:43
  P.M. on Tuesday, January 16, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Chan.

  CITY ATTORNEY ANNOUNCEMENT

  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz announced that Mayor Harrington would not be
  attending the meeting due to a COVID exposure and the City's inability to meet the
  technical requirements required by recent legislation for his remote participation.

  ROLL CALL

I  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, and Vice Mayor
  John Wu .
  Council Members Absent:  John R. Harrington.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director
  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark; Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Finance Director William
  Kaholokula, Community Development Director Aldo
  Cervantes, Police Chief Edwin Elizalde, and Assistant City
  Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

I  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Vice Mayor Wu announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF NEW COMMUNITY EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAM (CERT)
  MEMBERS

  Fire Engineer Takahiro Suzuki made the presentation.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 6  January 16, 2024
   3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Jacqueline Candelaria, resident, provided comments expressing concern about recent
  dog attacks.

  Barbara Messina, President of Soroptimist of Alhambra, San Gabriel, San Marino,
  invited Council to their 90th-year celebration event.

I  Andrew, resident, commented on Assembly Bill 481 and Policy 707 in relation to law
  enforcement use of military equipment and an annual Police Department report.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, and Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR)
  Commission Chair, thanked the City Council for the thoughtful appointments to the
  HEAR Commission earlier in the evening; reported on a recent trip to the Japanese-
  American National Museum by HEAR Commissioners and City staff; and commented
  on the HEAR Commission's annual work plan under consideration for Council
  approval.

  Cynthia Talavera, resident, commented on recent dog attacks and questioned who was
  responsible for receiving complaints related to dog attacks

  City Manager Lazzaretto, in response to public comments, explained that the City is
  working with animal control to determine where responsibilities lie and to please
  report non-emergency animal incidents to City Hall, and that the annual report on the
  AB 481 Policy is scheduled for the HEAR Commission in January and will be brought
  to the City Council in February.

I  4. CONSENT CALENDAR
  Regarding Item 4F, Marjan Abubo, representing SAFER, provided comments  in
  opposition.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4G as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  HARRINGTON

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of
  December 19, 2023.

I  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved December 8, 2023, December 14, 2023, December 21,
  2023, and December 28, 2023, Registers of Demands and Warrants for the payment
  of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - DECEMBER 2023

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for December
  2023.
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  January 16, 2024
   D. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH CALIFORNIA CONSULTING FOR
  GRANT WRITING SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $55,200 ANNUALLY

  The City Council approved the Professional Services Agreement with California
  Consulting for Grant Writing Services and authorized the City Manager to execute
  the agreement and issue a purchase order in the amount of $50,000.

  E. ORDINANCE NO. 699 APPROVING AN ANNEXATION AND PRE-ZONING AT

I  5623 NORTH GLADYS AVENUE (ANX23-001/ZC23-001/GPA23-001) -
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 699 entitled, "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Approving
  Planning Case Nos. ANX23-001, GPA23-001, and ZC23-001, Approving an
  annexation and pre-zoning at 5623 North Gladys Avenue."

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 700: AMENDING AN EXISTING PLANNED DEVELOPMENT
  OVERLAY ZONE AND APPROVING A DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR A
  MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT AT 201-217 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD
  (ZC22-001 AND DA22-001) - SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 700 entitled, "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Approving
  Planning Case Nos. ZC22-001 and DA22-001, Amending an Existing Planned
  Development Overlay Zone and Approving a Development Agreement for a
  Mixed-Use Development at 201-217 South San Gabriel Boulevard."

I  G. HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION PROPOSED
  2024 ANNUAL WORK PLAN

  The City Council received and filed the HEAR Commission 's 2024 Annual Workplan.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION AND DIRECTION ON A NEW SISTER CITY
  AND FRIENDSHIP CITY POLICY FOR THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation.

  Andrew, resident, requested that the policy include a provision to exclude countries
  that are adversaries to the United States.

  Discussion included funding in the annual budget for Friendship/Sister City

I  expenses; the implementation process; opposition to including verbiage about
  adversarial nations, appreciation for the policy having a local group take
  responsibility, travel will not be funded by the taxpayers, historical purpose of the
  program; benefits of cultural sharing; possible outside funding sources; exclusion
  of countries listed by the U.S. Department of State as hostile to the U.S.; partnering
  with the San Gabriel Tourism and Marketing Improvement District (TMID) for
  receptions, and equivalent gift exchanges.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ding, seconded by Council Member Chan,
  to adopt the policy presented, with a wording amendment to section 7.0 City
  Responsibilities to add that funds spent on meetings, receptions, and gifts for sister
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  January 16, 2024
   city delegations will be negligible unless an expenditure line item is added to a
  future annual City budget or unless approved on a case-by-case basis by the City
  Council.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

I  ABSENT:  HARRINGTON

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AUTHORIZATION OF  AN  ADDITIONAL  EVIDENCE  AND  PROPERTY
  TECHNICIAN (EPT)

  Police Sergeant Nhat Huynh made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included the process to review body-worn camera footage,

  Andrew, resident, questioned whether salary comparisons for this position were
  made with comparable cities.

  Discussion included the current competitive environment for police positions; the
  cost for the proposed position includes the value of benefits; technician workload
  and challenges providing information requested by the District Attorney's Office;
  training and skills required; timeline for hiring; effect on the need for this position
  if there is a change of District Attorney; use of Artificial Intelligence (Al); alternate

I  duties for technicians; cost for body-worn camera software; and that this item is to
  consider adding another position in an existing classification.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to adopt Resolution No. 24-01 and authorized the City Manager to approve
  the addition of a second Evidence and Property Technician for the San Gabriel
  Police Department.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  HARRINGTON

  B. PRESENTATION AND ACCEPTANCE OF THE ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE
  FINANCIAL REPORT AND OTHER AUDIT REPORTS FOR THE FISCAL VEAR
  ENDED JUNE 30, 2023
